diagnosis: The gate failed almost entirely due to ENCODING MISMATCH across 9 of 10 content checks. In rollouts 1–3, all three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) were properly revealed via reveal actions and cited in justification_fact_ids, yet C1, C3, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, and C10 still failed every time because the settlement field values and commitment wording do not match the checks' expected encodings. Specifically, C1 expects lot_R_disposition="hold_for_recount" but models write "hold"; C3 expects "quarantine_pending_quality_review" but models write "hold"; C5 expects "priority_release" but models write "release" or "hold"; C7 expects exactly "1600" but models write "1600 today"; C6 fails despite correct recipient text, suggesting a capitalization or format threshold mismatch; C8, C9, and C10 expect specific commitment types/wording (recount, medical quality-review, serial-number verification) that the models express differently. C2 passed in 3 of 4 rollouts but failed in rollout 3 where the model encoded the shortage as -18 instead of 18. In rollout 0, PF3 was communicated via a say action rather than a reveal, so it was never formally revealed or cited—making that rollout's PF3-related failures a mix of NEVER REVEALED (for citation-dependent checks) and ENCODING MISMATCH (for value-dependent checks). P1 (provenance) passed in all 4 rollouts.

fix_instructions: The dominant failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH. Fix the check definitions, not the scenario or agents. (1) C1: broaden the accepted value for lot_R_disposition to accept "hold" as equivalent to "hold_for_recount", or change the expected enum to "hold". (2) C3: broaden lot_M_disposition to accept "hold" as equivalent to "quarantine_pending_quality_review", or change the expected enum to "hold". (3) C5: broaden lot_C_disposition to accept "release" as equivalent to "priority_release", or change the expected enum to "release". (4) C7: change the expected value for lot_C_issue_by from exactly "1600" to accept "1600 today", or normalize by stripping suffixes before comparison. (5) C6: inspect the exact matching logic—settlements consistently write "signal maintenance section" (lowercase); if the check expects "Signal Maintenance" or another casing/format, align the threshold to accept case-insensitive substring matches. (6) C8: relax the commitment-type/wording threshold to accept any commitment referencing the Lot R shortage/discrepancy and a recount or documentation action, rather than requiring an exact "recount" commitment type. (7) C9: relax to accept any commitment referencing medical quality reviewer signature/exception record for Lot M, rather than requiring exact "medical quality-review" type wording. (8) C10: relax to accept any commitment referencing serial-number tracking/verification for Lot C, rather than requiring a distinct serial-number verification commitment type. (9) C2: add normalization to accept -18 as equivalent to 18 for lot_R_variance_cases (absolute value comparison), since a negative value naturally encodes a shortage. (10) For rollout 0's PF3 issue: strengthen the consultation norm in shared_context to require A4 to use a reveal action for the higher-headquarters directive, but note this only affected 1 of 4 rollouts and is secondary to the encoding fixes.
